title: Start an Agent Session in GCP
subtitle: Advanced · Claude Code and OpenCode

scenes.title: Place the terminal in GCP
scenes.body: Establish the workspace before running a client.
scenes.code:
Corporate GCP workspace
Training checkout: /work/training-orders
Clients: Claude Code and OpenCode
scenes.narration: Before we launch either agent, look at the workspace badge. It says Corporate G C P, and the terminal is open in that workspace. That's the operating boundary for this series. The repository in the demo is a synthetic order service. We'll start with a read-only task, so by the end you can compare exactly what the agent explored with what changed on disk.

scenes.title: Check the working directory
scenes.body: The next three commands establish the starting state.
scenes.code:
pwd
git status --short --branch
git rev-parse --short HEAD
scenes.narration: In the terminal, run P W D, then Git status and Git rev-parse. The path ends in training-orders. Status displays the lab branch and no file entries beneath it, so we have a clean starting point. The short commit is twenty-seven E four A B one. Copy the commit from your own terminal. You can use it later to reproduce the same inspection.
scenes.action: Check the directory, status, and commit.

scenes.title: Identify the installed clients
scenes.body: The installed build determines which controls you can check.
scenes.result:
Claude Code version: copy from terminal
OpenCode version: copy from terminal
scenes.narration: Now ask each client for its version. This is much faster than guessing from the menu or from a video. Record the two values your workspace reports. If one command is missing, you can finish the first inspection with the other approved client. Use those version numbers when you look up configuration, model selection, or skill discovery later.

scenes.title: Record the resolved model
scenes.body: Record the resolved identifier where the client displays it.
scenes.code:
Client: Claude Code or OpenCode
Resolved model: from authorized session
Provider: from approved workspace settings
Runtime: corporate GCP workspace
scenes.result: Lab record fields · use your workspace values
scenes.narration: Open the existing session's model selector or status view. Suppose the client shows a friendly model label. Record the resolved identifier when the workspace makes it visible, since the same label can point to different versions. Then check the configured provider. The terminal runs in G C P, while the configured provider determines where model requests are processed. Keep both facts in the session record.

scenes.title: Confirm what the session may do
scenes.body: The listed grants belong to the synthetic lab.
scenes.code:
Read training files       allowed
Edit the training branch  ask first
Run unit tests            ask first
External integrations     unavailable
scenes.result: First task scope: inspect the checkout
scenes.narration: Here is the effective policy for our example: reading the training files is allowed, and edits or unit-test runs ask for confirmation. Look up the effective policy for your own session. This matters even for a simple prompt. You can tell an agent to inspect a file, but a proposed command is still a separate action that needs to fit the session's permissions.

scenes.title: Begin with a read-only task
scenes.body: Use specific evidence the learner can open independently.
scenes.code:
Find the order quantity validator and its unit tests.
Point to the zero-quantity case with its file path.
Use read-only inspection for this request.
scenes.narration: Ask the agent for two paths and one concrete case: the quantity validator, its test file, and the test for zero. Watch it inspect the checkout. The example points to the validator in orders slash quantity dot P Y and to test rejects zero in the test suite. Those names give us a simple way to confirm the answer ourselves.
scenes.focus: Find the validator and its zero-case test
scenes.action: Send the inspection request in one approved client.

scenes.title: Verify the paths and starting state
scenes.body: The no-edit claim has a visible check.
scenes.narration: Open the reported validator and the test. Check that the test actually passes zero to the validator and expects a rejection. Then run the branch and commit checks again. In the demonstration the branch header is still the only status line, and the commit is unchanged. That gives us direct evidence about the checkout, independent of the agent's summary.

scenes.body: Keep enough information for another teammate to repeat it.

Workspace · branch · commit

scenes.result: Lab complete: two paths verified, clean checkout
scenes.narration: Finish by saving the workspace, commit, client version, model, provider, and permissions next to the two verified paths. That's the minimum useful record for the next lab. You can now start a session with a clear boundary, ask a small question, and verify the answer. Next, we'll check how both clients pick up the same repository convention.
